Subject: Questions on routing fallback, UK addendum, and retention (redlines attached)

Jordan —

Thanks for taking this on. We received Redwood's standard DPA but a few items are blocking our internal signoff: primarily around cross-border fallback behavior and retention of access logs. Specific asks from our privacy and procurement teams: 

- Can you confirm which transfer mechanisms Redwood intends to rely on for EU->US routing? We saw references to SCCs and also a UK addendum in your materials; please be explicit.
- For customers that require an onshore fallback (e.g., temporarily routing through US-based infra), do you have an operational TIA/DTIA-style control and a short description we can include in our addendum?
- Our legal team redlined the DPA for log retention and subprocessor snapshot requirements — please find the redlines attached (dpa_redlined_aurelia_20280328.pdf).
- We also need a transfer matrix that maps data flows, subprocessors, and regional fallbacks so we can complete our privacy impact assessment.

Can you provide a short written response we can include in our change control note, and ideally a one-hour call this week to walk legal/privacy through the transfer matrix?

Thanks,

Marta Ruiz
Privacy Program Manager
Aurelia Health

Attachments: dpa_redlined_aurelia_20280328.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Mar 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on routing fallback, UK addendum, and retention (redlines attached)

Marta — thanks for the clear list. Long answer short: Redwood supports SCCs and the UK IDTA/UK addendum where applicable, and we can operationalize an onshore fallback under a documented DTIA/TIA control model with compensating safeguards. I've attached a concise transfer matrix and a one-page UK addendum summary for your legal team.

Key points you can include in your change control note: 

1) Transfer mechanisms: Primary: EU SCCs (Model Clauses). Secondary: UK IDTA / UK Addendum for UK-origin data. Fallback: transient routing to US-hosted capacity is treated as a transient international access (TIA/DTIA) event and is governed by the DTIA playbook below.

2) DTIA/TIA operational controls (summary):
- Short-lived routing: fallback windows are time-limited and only used when latency or capacity issues would materially impact service.
- Data minimization: requests routed via fallback will only carry the processing tokens required for inference; no permanent replication of customer datasets to the fallback region.
- Cryptographic protections: TLS in transit and envelope encryption at rest; customer-managed KMS available for Private/Dedicated deployments.
- Access controls & logging: all administrative and control-plane access recorded; token-level tracing retained per retention policy.

3) Logs & retention: default hosted retention for user-facing access logs is 12 months. For Dedicated/Private customers we can offer extended retention (24 months) as a contractual amendment. We can produce a redacted sample of access logs and auditor CSVs for your PIAs.

4) Subprocessors & snapshot: we'll provide a current subprocessor snapshot (CSV) and a simple change-notice process; any changes that materially affect routing will be notified 30 days prior in accordance with the DPA.

Next steps I propose: 
- See attached: redwood_transfer_matrix.xlsx and uk_addendum_summary.pdf.
- I'll book a 60-minute call with you + Aurelia legal + our Privacy/Compliance team tomorrow afternoon — please confirm availability.
- If the retention redline is essential for signoff, Laura can propose a DocuSign amendment for a 24-month retention on Dedicated capacity (we'll include an explicit DTIA section).

If helpful I pasted the key parts below and have also copied our privacy ops lead (Kimberly) to confirm log sample availability.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer — Privacy & Compliance

Marta — quick follow up from the ops side. Jordan's summary is correct; a couple of operational clarifications we should call out explicitly for your security/privacy team: 

- Proofs we can provide: redacted access-log extracts (time window, request path, model ID), control-plane audit CSVs (who/when), and a sample syslog export demonstrating routing changes. I attached a short extract from our policy (log_retention_policy_extract.txt) for reference.
- Retention tiers: Hosted API (default) = 12 months for token-level traces and aggregated metrics; Dedicated = 24 months available by contract; Private = customer-dictated retention (we can disable retention if requested).
- Subprocessor timing: subprocessor snapshot provided as CSV; push-notice for material routing changes (>=30 days). For emergency fallback events (failover) we stamp the event in the audit chain and provide an after-action summary.

If Aurelia needs cryptographic separation, we can enable customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private. For hosted accounts we offer per-tenant encryption keys with limited exportability.

I'll join the call and can bring a redacted log sample.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Product Manager — Privacy Ops
